analysis.investment_thesis: Meesho is a Magic Formula dead-end — negative EBIT (-578 Cr in FY25) makes both Earnings Yield and ROIC incalculable, and the stock trades at 6.5x revenue with no path to near-term profitability. The FY25 net loss exploded to -3,942 Cr (vs. -328 Cr in FY24), signaling deep structural unprofitability despite strong revenue growth.
key_strengths: Revenue growth: 5,735 → 9,390 Cr over 2 years (~64%), indicating real business scale
Operating FCF turned positive: +186 Cr (FY24) and +516 Cr (FY25), suggesting cash burn is narrowing at the operating level
Near-zero debt (58 Cr borrowings vs. 74,700 Cr market cap), so financial distress risk is low
key_risks: Magic Formula cannot be applied — negative EBIT (-578 Cr) means Earnings Yield and ROIC are both negative; this stock is structurally uninvestable under my framework
Massively overvalued: EV ~74,611 Cr on -578 Cr EBIT and P/B of 50x on rapidly eroding equity (2,472 → 1,446 Cr in 2 years)
FY25 net loss of -3,942 Cr (vs. -328 Cr in FY24) driven by -835 Cr 'Other Income' swing — accounting optics mask potential one-time charges or fair-value losses
red_flags: Negative EBIT for all 3 years — Magic Formula is inapplicable by design
P/B of 50.42 on a company with shrinking, negative-trending equity
Net loss jumped 12x in FY25 to -3,942 Cr — major deterioration
Promoter stake only 16.57% — very low skin in the game
Other Income swung from +231 Cr to -835 Cr in one year — unexplained 1,066 Cr deterioration
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From the Magic Formula's perspective, Meesho is a non-starter. Earnings Yield = EBIT/EV = -578/74,611 = -0.77%, and ROIC is negative across all three years (ROCE of -8.71%). The formula ranks companies on two factors — cheap AND good — and Meesho fails both: it is expensive (6.5x sales, 50x book) and destroys capital. My framework was built for businesses earning high returns on tangible capital; a company burning -578 Cr at the operating line with negative working capital returns has no place in a Magic Formula screen.

The one silver lining is that operating cash flow turned positive (+539 Cr in FY25) while capex is negligible (-23 Cr), suggesting unit economics may be improving at the transaction layer. But the accounting P&L remains deeply negative, equity is eroding fast (down 41% in two years), and the FY25 net loss explosion (-3,942 Cr) raises serious questions about hidden write-downs or fair-value losses buried in "Other Income." At 74,700 Cr market cap with no visible EBIT breakeven horizon, the market is pricing in a venture-style outcome that Magic Formula investing explicitly avoids.
